cells.tense: You are here with your hand on the pen, feeling your way forward and letting the next step be enough.
cells.ask: keep choosing by what genuinely moves you, one step at a time, and notice what that builds when you let it build
cells.core:
When this goes well, you walk into things you can't see the end of — not because the fog lifted, but because you feel enough about the ground ahead to move onto it. You sense what's forming before it's confirmed, and you let that sense steer. You meet what's unclear as if it might be interesting rather than dangerous, and that turns out to be a way of finding out. The people near you can feel it; you're not waiting for permission from the unknown.

That way of moving has a direction of its own now. When you keep acting from what honestly engages you, the pull gets steadier and lasts longer, and this becomes something you can keep doing instead of a burst.
cells.sheetLine: You feel your way through what isn't clear yet, and you follow it.
cells.verb: Sensing what hasn't happened yet and stepping with that feeling as your guide
cells.place: in the part of a life where the path shows up one stretch at a time, never the whole road

cells.tense: You are out ahead of it, living in a version of how this goes that hasn't arrived and can't be written in advance.
cells.ask: tend one actual thing in front of you with your hands, and let care that doesn't clutch show you the pace
cells.core:
At its best this is the part of you that can stand inside not-knowing and still take the next right step — reading what's forming, moving toward it before it's proven. You can hold an unclear situation open long enough for its shape to show itself, and that patience is not passivity; it is how the path gets revealed, and you are good at it.

Right now you're reading ahead of the moment. Somewhere out there is a picture of how this resolves, and you're already living in it — rehearsing the ending, checking it against how it might go wrong, trying to lock the whole road down before you've walked it. The seeing is still good. The bracing is costing you the very thing you're trying to see. Something real and small is in front of you; giving it plain, unhurried care — the kind that doesn't grip — brings you back to where the next step actually is.

cells.tense: You stopped feeling your way through this some time back, and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: listen closely to one thing you don't already understand, this week, and let what you notice do the guiding
cells.core:
When it's working, this is the part of you that can move through uncertainty without forcing it closed — enough light for the next step, never enough to see the whole road, and you trust that and go. You notice what's forming, you let it stay unclear a little longer, and the way forward keeps showing up because you're not demanding it early.

That's not what's happening now. Nothing ahead gets the benefit of your sense of it. You wait for it to be clear before you let yourself feel anything about it, and it never gets clear that way, and so you've stopped walking. The capacity hasn't gone anywhere. Being genuinely curious about one thing you don't have figured out gives your sensing somewhere to land, and the quiet moving-through starts again from there.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped trusting what you sense about what's ahead.

cells.tense: You are already reading the room and steering by what you feel in it, and you're calling that just paying attention.
cells.ask: put one small practice around what you already perceive, and let doing it regularly show you it was yours
cells.core:
This capacity at its best is a real instrument: you sense what's forming before it's said, which way the wind is going, what the next stretch will ask of you — and you let that inform how you move. It is not guesswork; it lands often enough that people rely on it without naming it, and you do too.

But you've been counting it as ordinary. It shapes how you decide every day, and you describe it the way you'd describe the weather — something that comes, not something you do. The reading is yours. Give it one steady, ordinary practice, the same small act done again and again, and it stops looking like something that happens to you and starts looking like something you do.
